metadata.title: FrontierAtlas: An Evidence-Grounded Atlas of Open Scientific Problems
metadata.subtitle: 100 unresolved questions across physics, chemistry, genetics, psychology, and physiology
metadata.editorial_status: Research synthesis; provisional open-status assessment. Verify sources and changes before scholarly reuse.

problems.title: 4D Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
problems.question: Can an interacting four-dimensional continuum Yang–Mills quantum field theory be constructed rigorously with a positive spectral mass gap?
problems.justification: The Standard Model uses non-Abelian gauge theory, but the full constructive proof is missing.
problems.bottleneck: Nonperturbative continuum limits, gauge invariance and uniform spectral estimates resist existing tools.
problems.direction: Study rigorously controlled lattice limits; isolate conditions preserving reflection positivity and a volume-independent gap.
problems.first_test: Prove a uniform bound on spectral gaps for an explicitly restricted class before attempting 4D continuum control.

problems.title: Unforced 3D Navier–Stokes regularity
problems.question: Do all smooth divergence-free finite-energy initial data yield global smooth unforced solutions, or can singularities form?
problems.justification: Resolving this would clarify a central issue in PDE theory and idealized fluid mechanics.
problems.bottleneck: Vortex stretching and supercritical estimates prevent known energy controls from bounding all gradients.
problems.direction: Seek scale-critical a priori estimates or exclude concentrated vorticity geometry; verify all claimed inequalities.
problems.first_test: Derive a new coercive inequality under a clearly stated symmetry or alignment condition.

problems.title: Quantum gravity with observable predictions
problems.question: Which mathematically consistent framework reproduces general relativity and quantum field theory in their domains and predicts a discriminating effect?
problems.justification: General relativity and quantum theory are independently predictive yet conceptually incomplete in combination.
problems.bottleneck: No accessible high-energy experimental regime and no unique model-selection principle.
problems.direction: Compare effective theories and semiclassical observables, including gravitationally mediated entanglement proposals.
problems.first_test: Specify an observable where two candidate frameworks give non-overlapping uncertainty intervals.

problems.title: Black-hole information dynamics
problems.question: How is unitary information recovery realized in realistic evaporating black holes beyond controlled idealizations?
problems.justification: It probes the compatibility of gravity, entropy, and quantum unitarity.
problems.bottleneck: Semiclassical calculations, interior reconstruction and boundary formulations differ in regimes of validity.
problems.direction: Analyze toy solvable models and identify operational observables robust to model assumptions.
problems.first_test: Establish a consistent information-recovery map for a constrained evaporation model without cloning.

problems.title: Origin of neutrino mass
problems.question: Why are neutrino masses extremely small, and are neutrinos Dirac or Majorana particles?
problems.justification: Oscillations show nonzero mass, beyond the minimal massless-neutrino Standard Model.
problems.bottleneck: Absolute scale and particle nature are not fixed by oscillation data.
problems.direction: Jointly constrain beta decay, neutrinoless double beta decay and cosmological mass bounds with theory priors explicit.
problems.first_test: Identify predictions differentiating two viable neutrino mass mechanisms in at least two observables.

problems.title: Neutrino mass ordering and CP phase
problems.question: What are the mass ordering and leptonic CP-violating phase with statistically robust global consistency?
problems.justification: These parameters affect flavor physics, oscillation predictions and leptogenesis hypotheses.
problems.bottleneck: Parameter degeneracies, detector systematics and tension across channels.
problems.direction: Use correlated joint fits with reactor, accelerator and atmospheric data and verified nuisance-model robustness.
problems.first_test: Demand consistent ordering and CP estimates across independent baseline/energy combinations.

problems.title: Cosmic matter–antimatter asymmetry
problems.question: Which interactions generated the observed baryon asymmetry while satisfying available particle constraints?
problems.justification: An initially symmetric universe requires a viable source of baryon-number asymmetry.
problems.bottleneck: Different baryogenesis scenarios share low-energy signatures and depend on uncertain early-universe conditions.
problems.direction: Build benchmark leptogenesis or electroweak scenarios, solve transport equations, and link to testable observables.
problems.first_test: Find allowed parameter regions with a measurable signature absent in a competing scenario.

problems.title: Strong CP problem
problems.question: Why is effective QCD CP violation so small, and does an axion or another mechanism explain it?
problems.justification: A tiny QCD theta parameter is a striking naturalness puzzle.
problems.bottleneck: Axion couplings are model dependent and broad parameter spaces evade detection.
problems.direction: Compare axion and non-axion scenarios using precision EDM constraints and astrophysical signatures.
problems.first_test: Derive a predictive relation between two independent observables rather than a single exclusion curve.

problems.title: Identity of dark matter
problems.question: What particle or alternative physical explanation accounts for cosmological and galactic dark-matter evidence?
problems.justification: Gravitational observations demand an explanation extending ordinary luminous matter.
problems.bottleneck: Indirect signatures are degenerate with astrophysical nuisance processes; null direct searches constrain candidates.
problems.direction: Combine lensing, structure formation and laboratory searches in shared parameterized models.
problems.first_test: Require a single candidate to match independent astrophysical scales and laboratory limits.

problems.title: Nature of accelerated expansion
problems.question: Is cosmic acceleration due to a cosmological constant, evolving dark energy or modified gravity?
problems.justification: The mechanism affects the history and possible fate of the universe.
problems.bottleneck: Distance, growth and geometry measurements have parameter and systematic degeneracies.
problems.direction: Jointly fit expansion and growth observables with reproducible systematics and nonparametric reconstruction.
problems.first_test: Find a forecastable observable that discriminates constant-w from evolving-w models.

problems.title: Hubble-constant tension
problems.question: Is the mismatch between local distance-ladder and early-universe H0 estimates a systematic artifact or new physics?
problems.justification: The discrepancy challenges the internal consistency of precision cosmology.
problems.bottleneck: Distance calibration and early-universe parameter assumptions are difficult to separate.
problems.direction: Cross-calibrate independent distance indicators and compute Bayesian evidence under matched systematics.
problems.first_test: Show whether independent late-time measurements converge under blind analyses.

problems.title: Amplitude-of-clustering discrepancies
problems.question: Do apparent S8 discrepancies arise from astrophysical calibration or altered growth of structure?
problems.justification: The growth amplitude probes cosmological composition and gravitational dynamics.
problems.bottleneck: Weak-lensing shear calibrations, baryonic feedback and analysis pipelines can shift inference.
problems.direction: Jointly analyze lensing, clustering and CMB with blinded nuisance priors; do not assume all surveys disagree.
problems.first_test: Quantify tension separately for each survey and robustness to baryonic feedback models.

problems.title: Microscopic mechanism of high-Tc pairing
problems.question: Which interactions produce superconducting pairing in strongly correlated unconventional materials?
problems.justification: A causal mechanism could enable predictive materials design rather than post-hoc models.
problems.bottleneck: Competing orders and strongly correlated electrons yield similar macroscopic signals.
problems.direction: Fit candidate Hamiltonians to spectroscopy, transport and controlled tuning experiments.
problems.first_test: Predict a new response to pressure or doping not used in fitting.

problems.title: Strange-metal transport universality
problems.question: Why do diverse correlated metals show non-Fermi-liquid transport, and which common mechanisms, if any, apply?
problems.justification: Strange metals expose failures of conventional quasiparticle descriptions.
problems.bottleneck: Finite-temperature scaling can fit several theories and material-specific disorder obscures universal structure.
problems.direction: Compare transport, optical probes and quantum critical scaling under independent perturbations.
problems.first_test: Recover scaling exponent and amplitude across at least two material families without refitting all parameters.

problems.title: Microscopic glass-transition dynamics
problems.question: What structures and dynamical pathways control extreme slowing down near glass formation?
problems.justification: Glassy dynamics occurs without ordinary long-range crystalline ordering.
problems.bottleneck: Rare rearrangements, finite observation windows and ambiguous structural descriptors.
problems.direction: Test interpretable state variables across model glass formers with out-of-distribution prediction.
problems.first_test: Predict relaxation time from structure at temperatures held out from training.

problems.title: Avalanche and plasticity in amorphous solids
problems.question: Can a predictive mesoscale theory recover yielding, shear localization and avalanches across disordered solids?
problems.justification: Failure of amorphous materials depends on collective microscale events.
problems.bottleneck: Disorder, finite-size effects and strongly history-dependent force chains.
problems.direction: Infer coarse-grained state variables and compare universality classes under cyclic and monotonic loading.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate transfer of avalanche statistics and yield predictions between material classes.

problems.title: Universal turbulence closure
problems.question: Can unresolved turbulent stresses be represented by stable, transferable closures across Reynolds numbers and geometries?
problems.justification: Reliable turbulent prediction is central to engineering and geophysical modeling.
problems.bottleneck: Scale interactions, anisotropy and nonlocal history defeat common closures.
problems.direction: Build invariance-preserving closures with energy stability and OOD flow tests.
problems.first_test: Prove a discrete energy bound and reproduce unseen separation and transition regimes.

problems.title: Solar coronal energy partition
problems.question: How much coronal heating comes from reconnection, waves and intermittent dissipation across solar conditions?
problems.justification: The million-kelvin solar corona requires sustained energy deposition.
problems.bottleneck: Line-of-sight mixing, unresolved events and incomplete magnetic measurements.
problems.direction: Combine multi-height spectroscopy with radiative MHD and explicit energy budgets.
problems.first_test: Predict temperature, nonthermal linewidths and temporal variability simultaneously.

problems.title: Fast magnetic reconnection across regimes
problems.question: What controls the onset and universal scaling of fast reconnection in collisional, collisionless and turbulent plasmas?
problems.justification: Reconnection drives energy release in astrophysics and laboratory plasma devices.
problems.bottleneck: Kinetic and fluid scales couple; reconnection rates depend on boundary and turbulence.
problems.direction: Compare kinetic simulations with reduced closures and laboratory diagnostics.
problems.first_test: Derive a regime map that predicts reconnection rate across transitions without retuning.

problems.title: Predictive fusion-plasma transport
problems.question: Can burning-plasma transport, disruptions and confinement be predicted reliably outside the training machine and operating regime?
problems.justification: Commercial fusion depends on stable confinement under complex coupled dynamics.
problems.bottleneck: Nonlinear turbulence, energetic-particle effects, wall interaction and rare disruptions.
problems.direction: Combine gyrokinetics, reduced physics models and uncertainty-aware validation on withheld discharges.
problems.first_test: Prospectively predict transport and disruption risk on another device with calibrated uncertainty.

problems.title: Out-of-distribution reaction prediction
problems.question: Can models predict product, yield and feasibility for new substrate families and new conditions?
problems.justification: Reaction screening remains costly despite successful in-domain machine-learning predictors.
problems.bottleneck: Published reactions are selection biased; negative results and hidden conditions are rare.
problems.direction: Use prospective split-by-scaffold and laboratory validation of calibrated predictions.
problems.first_test: Compare predicted yield intervals with blinded unseen reaction families.

problems.title: Predictive transition-state discovery
problems.question: Can reaction pathways and activation free energies be discovered without prespecifying likely transition states?
problems.justification: Rate predictions and mechanistic discrimination depend on pathways rather than just products.
problems.bottleneck: Potential-energy landscapes are combinatorially large and solvent changes barrier structure.
problems.direction: Couple reactive dynamics, active-learning potentials and verified saddle-point calculations.
problems.first_test: Recover known barriers then prospectively predict a pathway unseen by mechanism templates.

problems.title: Solvent and microenvironment selectivity
problems.question: How do solvent structure, ions and confinement jointly determine regio-, chemo- and stereoselectivity?
problems.justification: Many selectivity reversals cannot be forecast by gas-phase mechanisms alone.
problems.bottleneck: Solvation free energies and molecular reorganization require correlated sampling.
problems.direction: Compare explicit-solvent free-energy simulations against controlled solvent-series experiments.
problems.first_test: Predict sign and magnitude of selectivity reversal under a pre-registered solvent swap.

problems.title: Mechanistic reaction-network inference
problems.question: Which elementary reactions and rate constants are distinguishable from partial time-series observations?
problems.justification: False mechanisms can fit identical macroscopic conversion curves.
problems.bottleneck: Structural non-identifiability and undetected intermediates are pervasive.
problems.direction: Derive identifiability conditions using sensitivity rank, isotope labels and designed pulse inputs.
problems.first_test: Produce a counterexample for inadequate sensors and recover parameters with the minimum added measurement.

problems.title: Active catalytic sites under operating conditions
problems.question: Which sites actually dominate catalytic turnover while catalysts restructure in reaction environments?
problems.justification: Ex situ structures may not represent active phases under bias, heat or gas exposure.
problems.bottleneck: Transient minority sites are invisible to ensemble characterization.
problems.direction: Use operando spectroscopy and isotope transient kinetics linked to microkinetic models.
problems.first_test: Predict turnover change following selective poisoning of a proposed active site.

problems.title: Dynamically driven catalysis
problems.question: When can periodic modulation genuinely improve rates or selectivity beyond optimal steady-state operation?
problems.justification: Time-varying catalysts challenge steady-state optimization assumptions.
problems.bottleneck: Driving-waveform cost, catalyst memory and resonance identification complicate comparison.
problems.direction: Use nonlinear periodic reaction-network theory and matched-energy dynamic/steady baselines.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate reproducible net gain after accounting for modulation energy and catalyst aging.

problems.title: Selective electrochemical CO2 conversion
problems.question: Can C2+ product selectivity, energy efficiency and catalyst stability be jointly optimized at practical current density?
problems.justification: Useful carbon conversion remains limited by competing pathways and economics.
problems.bottleneck: Local pH, mass transfer, reconstruction and product crossover change apparent kinetics.
problems.direction: Unify microkinetics with transport and operando product quantitation in full cells.
problems.first_test: Predict Faradaic efficiency and stability at a withheld operating current and electrolyte.

problems.title: Ambient nitrogen reduction attribution
problems.question: Can genuinely catalytic nitrogen-to-ammonia synthesis be unambiguously distinguished from contamination and background sources?
problems.justification: Ambient nitrogen fixation would transform sustainable fertilizer production if validated at practical rates.
problems.bottleneck: Trace nitrogen impurities and false-positive ammonia assays confound many low-rate claims.
problems.direction: Use isotopically labeled nitrogen, rigorous blanks, mass balance and independent analytical methods.
problems.first_test: Show reproducible isotope-verified formation with closed nitrogen balance and energy accounting.

problems.title: Reliable strong-correlation electronic energies
problems.question: Can affordable computational chemistry predict chemically accurate energetics for strongly correlated open-shell systems?
problems.justification: Catalysts and transition-metal complexes commonly defeat single-reference approximations.
problems.bottleneck: Many-body Hilbert-space growth and ambiguous reference states limit accuracy.
problems.direction: Benchmark systematically against controlled small systems and high-level solvers with uncertainty bounds.
problems.first_test: Set a prospective error target for spin-state gaps on an external benchmark.

problems.title: Electrode–electrolyte interphase formation
problems.question: What coupled reactions determine SEI/CEI composition and long-term passivation?
problems.justification: Battery safety, life and efficiency depend on transient interfacial chemistry.
problems.bottleneck: Buried interphases evolve dynamically and involve reactive low-abundance components.
problems.direction: Couple operando diagnostics with reaction-network models and sensitivity-based experiment design.
problems.first_test: Predict changes in gas evolution and film composition after an electrolyte perturbation.

problems.title: Nucleation pathway selection
problems.question: Which molecular clusters determine polymorph and nucleation rate across solvents and interfaces?
problems.justification: Crystal form controls drug and functional-material properties.
problems.bottleneck: Rare nucleation events and nonclassical pathways are poorly sampled.
problems.direction: Use rare-event simulation with in situ scattering under controlled supersaturation.
problems.first_test: Predict polymorph selection when solvent or confinement changes, not just fit observed final crystals.

problems.title: Predictive electrochemical material degradation
problems.question: Can lifetime, failure modes and interfacial side reactions be extrapolated from accelerated tests?
problems.justification: Accelerated cycling does not necessarily preserve the mechanism of real operation.
problems.bottleneck: Coupled electrochemical-mechanical pathways and hidden state variables.
problems.direction: Use mechanistic state-space models and post-mortem chemical validation across operating conditions.
problems.first_test: Predict a withheld real-use aging trajectory from accelerated data with uncertainty coverage.

problems.title: Plausible prebiotic feedstock integration
problems.question: Can geochemically plausible settings supply and sustain enough compatible precursors for subsequent chemistry?
problems.justification: Isolated syntheses do not establish a sustainable reaction ecology.
problems.bottleneck: Mutually incompatible pH, temperature, UV and reagent conditions.
problems.direction: Integrate geochemical flow-reactor experiments with mass-balanced kinetic networks.
problems.first_test: Sustain target intermediates under an internally consistent cycle without unrealistic purification.

problems.title: Origin of biological homochirality
problems.question: Which mechanism produced and preserved molecular enantiomeric enrichment before biology?
problems.justification: Biological polymers exhibit pronounced handedness without a confirmed prebiotic origin pathway.
problems.bottleneck: Amplification can require narrow environments; initial bias and racemization are uncertain.
problems.direction: Test coupled autocatalysis and compartment models under geologically plausible feedstocks.
problems.first_test: Achieve robust amplification under variable starting biases and environmental cycling.

problems.title: Coupling replication and metabolism
problems.question: What minimal chemical network can self-maintain, replicate and support Darwinian evolution?
problems.justification: Independent demonstrations of replication or metabolism do not establish an integrated evolvable system.
problems.bottleneck: Resource competition, error accumulation and side reactions can destabilize networks.
problems.direction: Build chemostat protocell experiments with explicit resource fluxes and heritable sequence variation.
problems.first_test: Show repeated selection over generations rather than a one-time amplification event.

problems.title: Stable protocell growth and division
problems.question: How can compartments grow, divide and transmit functional components without modern enzymes?
problems.justification: Heritable chemistry requires physical compartments with coupled internal reactions.
problems.bottleneck: Osmotic stress, permeability and unequal partitioning impair propagation.
problems.direction: Construct coupled membrane-growth and reaction–diffusion models with experimental vesicle cycles.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate multiple generations retaining chemical function and material balance.

problems.title: General laws of chemical self-organization
problems.question: Which constraints make dissipative reaction networks produce stable, function-bearing structures?
problems.justification: Complex chemical organization often depends on continuous energy throughput.
problems.bottleneck: Kinetic nonlinearities and multiple steady states complicate broad organizing principles.
problems.direction: Analyze bifurcations, entropy production and chemical reaction network invariants in controlled systems.
problems.first_test: Predict the onset and failure of self-sustaining organization from independently estimated parameters.

problems.title: Secondary organic aerosol molecular closure
problems.question: Can emission-to-aerosol transformation and aging be predicted from molecularly resolved mechanisms?
problems.justification: Atmospheric aerosol affects health, radiation and cloud interactions.
problems.bottleneck: Thousands of oxidized compounds and multiphase reactions challenge comprehensive measurement.
problems.direction: Combine chamber kinetics, high-resolution mass spectrometry and transport-aware chemistry.
problems.first_test: Predict aerosol yield and oxidation state for an unseen precursor mixture.

problems.title: Multiphase atmospheric oxidation
problems.question: How do radicals, particle phase and humidity control aging pathways in realistic atmospheres?
problems.justification: Many atmospheric models simplify heterogeneous oxidative chemistry.
problems.bottleneck: Surface and bulk reactions are difficult to separate experimentally.
problems.direction: Use isotopic tracers, controlled humidity and diffusion-reaction models.
problems.first_test: Correctly predict kinetic regime changes as particle viscosity and size vary.

problems.title: Closed-loop sustainable polymer chemistry
problems.question: Which recyclable polymer architectures can satisfy durability, separation, depolymerization and energy constraints simultaneously?
problems.justification: Chemical recyclability can trade off with performance and lifecycle benefit.
problems.bottleneck: Mixture contamination and process-energy accounting undermine ideal-lab claims.
problems.direction: Optimize polymer design with reaction thermodynamics plus realistic material-flow analysis.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate repeated mixed-stream recycling with retained properties and validated lifecycle gains.

problems.title: Variant-to-target-gene assignment
problems.question: Which distal regulatory variant changes which gene in a relevant cell state?
problems.justification: Most associated regions are not directly interpretable as gene-level mechanisms.
problems.bottleneck: Chromatin proximity and expression correlation are not enough to establish causal links.
problems.direction: Integrate allele-specific perturbations, enhancer screens and chromatin contacts across cell states.
problems.first_test: Correctly predict target-gene changes for held-out precise edits.

problems.title: Combinatorial enhancer grammar
problems.question: Can enhancer sequence rules predict transcriptional effects of new combinations of motifs?
problems.justification: A predictive regulatory code would enable mechanistic interpretation and design.
problems.bottleneck: Context dependence and epistasis between binding motifs challenge simple sequence models.
problems.direction: Test motif insertion/deletion libraries and out-of-distribution enhancer predictions.
problems.first_test: Predict a held-out multi-motif perturbation series in two cell types.

problems.title: Causal function of 3D genome organization
problems.question: When does changing genome folding alter expression versus reflect downstream transcriptional state?
problems.justification: Chromosomal contact maps are often used as causal proxies.
problems.bottleneck: Correlated topology and gene activity may both respond to third factors.
problems.direction: Perturb boundaries and loop anchors with time-resolved nascent RNA and structural mapping.
problems.first_test: Predict expression changes under matched contact-changing and contact-neutral edits.

problems.title: Splicing-code generalization across tissue
problems.question: Can noncoding sequence changes predict cell-specific splice isoforms and downstream phenotypes?
problems.justification: Aberrant splicing explains many disease-associated variants not captured by simple coding annotations.
problems.bottleneck: Long-range context and RNA-binding proteins vary between tissues.
problems.direction: Link sequence-based models to minigene and endogenous editing assays across differentiated cell types.
problems.first_test: Predict isoform shifts for new variants in previously unseen cell contexts.

problems.title: Rare-to-common architecture of complex traits
problems.question: How do common, rare and structural variants jointly shape trait variance and risk?
problems.justification: Different variant classes are observed with different sensitivity and ascertainment.
problems.bottleneck: Frequency-dependent effects and population structure create unstable variance decomposition.
problems.direction: Use ancestry-aware whole-genome models and family-based validation.
problems.first_test: Predict incremental variance explained in independently sequenced families, not just training cohorts.

problems.title: Higher-order epistasis inference
problems.question: Which gene interactions beyond pairs alter phenotype under realistic genetic backgrounds?
problems.justification: Nonadditivity may expose regulatory and protein-network mechanisms.
problems.bottleneck: Interaction search spaces explode and power is limited for rare combinations.
problems.direction: Combine combinatorial CRISPR designs with sparse hierarchical statistical models.
problems.first_test: Prospectively predict triple perturbation phenotypes from lower-order training.

problems.title: Gene–environment causal interactions
problems.question: Which genetic effects change under modifiable exposures, rather than reflecting confounding or reverse causation?
problems.justification: Environmental context can alter biological response to the same variant.
problems.bottleneck: Exposure error, socioeconomic structure and reverse causality blur interactions.
problems.direction: Use within-family designs, exposure perturbations and repeated biomarker measures.
problems.first_test: Replicate an interaction in a separately randomized or quasi-experimental setting.

problems.title: Transportability of genetic risk estimates
problems.question: When and why do polygenic predictions lose calibration across ancestry, age, environment and care systems?
problems.justification: Unequal reliability can worsen health disparities and distort decisions.
problems.bottleneck: Linkage disequilibrium, allele frequency, environment and phenotype definition vary.
problems.direction: Develop multi-population recalibration with subgroup uncertainty and prospective validation.
problems.first_test: Prespecify calibration and clinical utility across independent demographic and ancestry continua.

problems.title: Unseen combinatorial perturbation effects
problems.question: Can cellular responses to combinations of untested gene interventions be predicted from sparse training?
problems.justification: Combinatorial screens scale exponentially and do not cover all cellular contexts.
problems.bottleneck: Nonlinear network rewiring and baseline cell states break model generalization.
problems.direction: Train on single and limited double perturbations; evaluate blinded combinations.
problems.first_test: Beat additive and nearest-neighbor baselines under split-by-gene-and-cell-context tests.

problems.title: Cell-fate branching and plasticity
problems.question: Which regulatory decisions make differentiation trajectories stable, reversible or branching?
problems.justification: Snapshot single-cell atlases cannot determine full transition mechanisms.
problems.bottleneck: Destructive measurement and hidden ancestry make trajectories ambiguous.
problems.direction: Combine live imaging, lineage barcodes and timed perturbation in state-space models.
problems.first_test: Predict fate distribution after a timed regulator knockout held out from fitting.

problems.title: Spatial cell–cell regulatory influence
problems.question: How can causal signaling between neighboring cells be distinguished from shared microenvironment?
problems.justification: Spatial transcriptomic neighborhoods provide correlations, not direct communication mechanisms.
problems.bottleneck: Many assays mix cells within spots and ligand-receptor expression is an indirect proxy.
problems.direction: Integrate higher-resolution mapping, spatial perturbations and diffusion-reaction models.
problems.first_test: Predict localized response to targeted cell ablation or ligand blocking.

problems.title: Cross-instrument and cross-tissue atlas alignment
problems.question: Can cell identities be matched reliably across platforms, tissue states and batches without erasing real biology?
problems.justification: Atlases must be harmonized before interpreting conserved pathways.
problems.bottleneck: Batch correction can collapse rare states or generate spurious equivalences.
problems.direction: Use known cell mixtures and orthogonal marker assays with uncertainty-aware alignment.
problems.first_test: Recover rare-state identities on entirely held-out tissues and platforms.

problems.title: Somatic mutation to tissue dysfunction
problems.question: Which age-acquired mutations directly drive inflammation and organ functional decline?
problems.justification: Somatic clones can be markers of aging and sometimes active causes of pathology.
problems.bottleneck: Clonal selection and environmental stress create feedback and confounding.
problems.direction: Perturb matched clones in organoids and combine lineage-resolved longitudinal sequencing.
problems.first_test: Separate mutation effects from clone-size effects on measured tissue function.

problems.title: Control and co-option of transposable elements
problems.question: When do transposable elements disrupt genomes, and when do they become beneficial regulatory elements?
problems.justification: A large fraction of mammalian DNA derives from mobile-element families.
problems.bottleneck: Repeat mapping is difficult and effects depend strongly on evolutionary context.
problems.direction: Combine long-read assemblies, locus-specific CRISPRi and cross-species reporter assays.
problems.first_test: Validate regulatory function for a formerly ambiguous repetitive locus.

problems.title: Complex structural-variant interpretation
problems.question: How do repeated-region structural variants alter phenotype in a dosage- and context-dependent manner?
problems.justification: Assembly advances reveal variants missed by short-read analysis.
problems.bottleneck: Repetitive regions and linked alleles confound causal attribution.
problems.direction: Use haplotype-resolved assemblies, engineered isogenic lines and long-range regulation assays.
problems.first_test: Resolve one region into sequence-specific, dosage and expression effects.

problems.title: Population-specific mutational processes
problems.question: Which environmental and repair pathways explain variation in somatic and germline mutation signatures?
problems.justification: Identifying mechanisms can help interpret cancer, aging and inherited variation.
problems.bottleneck: Several processes yield overlapping spectra and exposure histories are incomplete.
problems.direction: Use experimentally controlled exposures and repair-deficient backgrounds with generative signature models.
problems.first_test: Correctly infer withheld causal exposure from a blinded mutation spectrum.

problems.title: Resolving variants of uncertain significance
problems.question: Can functional evidence reliably classify rare variants for clinically relevant decisions?
problems.justification: Many detected variants lack enough evidence to be labeled benign or pathogenic.
problems.bottleneck: Assays do not always replicate native tissues or clinical penetrance.
problems.direction: Calibrate multiplexed functional assays against clinically curated variants and segregation data.
problems.first_test: Prospectively classify blinded variants with calibrated error and clinically meaningful utility.

problems.title: Detecting low-frequency mosaicism
problems.question: Which somatic variants exist in restricted tissues and actually cause disease?
problems.justification: Mosaic mutations may be absent from routinely sampled blood.
problems.bottleneck: Low allele fraction, tissue sampling and sequencing artifacts reduce sensitivity.
problems.direction: Design multi-tissue error-corrected assays and mechanistic organoid validation.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate robust detection and tissue-phenotype concordance using orthogonal methods.

problems.title: Long-term genomic editing safety
problems.question: Can intended edits be separated from rare off-target, structural and clonal consequences over years?
problems.justification: Therapeutic editing may produce delayed effects not represented in short cell-culture assays.
problems.bottleneck: Rare event detection and long latency require extensive follow-up.
problems.direction: Combine long-read sequencing, single-cell lineage tracing and function-specific safety assays.
problems.first_test: Prespecify a detection limit for rearrangements and track clonal dynamics longitudinally.

problems.title: Context-dependent pharmacogenomic effects
problems.question: When do genotype-based drug-response predictions remain valid across co-medications, physiology and populations?
problems.justification: Genetic effects on metabolism may depend on non-genetic context.
problems.bottleneck: Variable dosing, adherence, organ function and population structure obscure interactions.
problems.direction: Combine pharmacokinetic models with prospective genotype-stratified data and metabolite assays.
problems.first_test: Show externally validated dosing benefit with adverse-event monitoring, beyond association.

problems.title: Discriminating neural theories of consciousness
problems.question: Which preregistered neural observations could decisively separate leading theories of conscious experience?
problems.justification: Existing theories explain overlapping data but make different anatomical and temporal predictions.
problems.bottleneck: Task demands and post-hoc interpretation can obscure theory-specific falsification.
problems.direction: Conduct adversarial multi-lab tests with matched modalities and explicit decision thresholds.
problems.first_test: Identify an observation that one formal theory excludes and another requires.

problems.title: Conscious content without behavioral report
problems.question: Which neural measures indicate experience without confusing it with attention, memory or motor reporting?
problems.justification: Clinical and experimental subjects may not provide reliable overt reports.
problems.bottleneck: Covert measures are indirect and their specificity cannot be guaranteed.
problems.direction: Triangulate no-report paradigms with validated report conditions and perturbations.
problems.first_test: Estimate false-positive and false-negative rates under controlled vigilance changes.

problems.title: Computational calibration of introspection
problems.question: What mechanisms govern the match between subjective confidence and actual performance?
problems.justification: Confidence guides real decisions and is altered in some mental disorders.
problems.bottleneck: Measures can reflect response bias and task difficulty rather than meta-accuracy.
problems.direction: Use hierarchical signal-detection models across tasks and controlled feedback.
problems.first_test: Predict confidence calibration on an unseen task using independent behavioral observables.

problems.title: Conscious state transitions
problems.question: Which neural dynamical variables govern reversible transitions across wakefulness, sleep and anesthesia?
problems.justification: Consciousness varies rapidly while recorded neural activity is high-dimensional.
problems.bottleneck: Changes in arousal, motor output and sensory responsiveness are correlated.
problems.direction: Fit dynamical systems to multi-modal recordings during controlled state changes.
problems.first_test: Prospectively predict transitions and recovery while controlling for sedation and sensory input.

problems.title: Mechanisms and limits of memory reconsolidation
problems.question: When does retrieval destabilize memory and permit lasting updating?
problems.justification: Changing maladaptive memories has important theoretical and clinical implications.
problems.bottleneck: Boundary conditions and some replication results remain inconsistent.
problems.direction: Preregister factorial tests varying reminder strength, memory age and prediction error.
problems.first_test: Predict a parameter region where updating succeeds and one where it cannot.

problems.title: Neural-to-cognitive memory representations
problems.question: How do changing neural engrams preserve stable recall while permitting flexible generalization?
problems.justification: Memories can persist despite neural representational drift.
problems.bottleneck: Population recordings sample only fragments of distributed representations.
problems.direction: Link longitudinal neural data, retrieval cues and causal ensemble perturbations.
problems.first_test: Predict behavioral recall after manipulating a neural subpopulation not used during model fitting.

problems.title: Generalizable exploration–exploitation models
problems.question: Can one mechanistic model explain human information seeking across risk, novelty and environmental change?
problems.justification: Models often fit a single laboratory bandit task but fail in other contexts.
problems.bottleneck: Latent objectives and learning rates are observationally confounded.
problems.direction: Use task families designed to orthogonalize uncertainty and reward.
problems.first_test: Predict trial-level behavior across a held-out environmental volatility regime.

problems.title: Transfer of abstract reasoning
problems.question: Why does relational or compositional knowledge sometimes generalize and sometimes remain task-specific?
problems.justification: Adaptive intelligence depends on recombining learned rules in new settings.
problems.bottleneck: Language familiarity, task practice and motivation are alternative explanations.
problems.direction: Design intervention experiments that separate trained relations from surface features.
problems.first_test: Predict compositional transfer to genuinely novel stimulus categories.

problems.title: Cross-cultural transport of psychological findings
problems.question: Which psychological effects hold across language, culture and social institutions?
problems.justification: Unrepresentative samples make population-level claims uncertain.
problems.bottleneck: Translated measures may not capture identical latent constructs.
problems.direction: Coordinate cross-cultural preregistered studies with measurement-invariance tests.
problems.first_test: Predefine effect-size equivalence thresholds across diverse sampling frames.

problems.title: Causal social-contagion mechanisms
problems.question: When does behavior spread by influence rather than homophily or shared exposure?
problems.justification: Correlated behavior in networks does not by itself establish peer causation.
problems.bottleneck: Network interference, friendship selection and external shocks confound observed cascades.
problems.direction: Use randomized exposure where ethical and infer causal mechanisms with network-aware estimators.
problems.first_test: Predict responses in untouched neighborhoods following an exogenous intervention.

problems.title: Mechanisms sustaining group polarization
problems.question: Which feedback loops generate stable intergroup divergence and when can they reverse?
problems.justification: Extreme group separation affects collective decisions.
problems.bottleneck: Algorithmic selection, social identity and exposure are correlated.
problems.direction: Compare causal network experiments with interpretable agent-based opinion dynamics.
problems.first_test: Predict a shift in distribution of opinions under a preregistered contact intervention.

problems.title: Belief formation from aggregated opinions
problems.question: When do ratings, polls and social consensus improve versus distort individual judgments?
problems.justification: People frequently treat other people's summarized judgments as evidence.
problems.bottleneck: Selection bias in who expresses an opinion can mimic actual consensus.
problems.direction: Randomize visibility and sample composition of aggregate signals.
problems.first_test: Quantify when aggregation changes calibration rather than merely agreement.

problems.title: Mechanistic dimensions across diagnoses
problems.question: Which continuous cognitive/affective dimensions predict impairment better than coarse symptom labels?
problems.justification: Diagnostic categories often combine biologically heterogeneous individuals.
problems.bottleneck: Measurement noise, comorbidity and changing state are difficult to separate.
problems.direction: Use longitudinal multi-task assessments and latent-state models externally validated.
problems.first_test: Predict cross-diagnostic functioning over time more accurately than symptom-count baselines.

problems.title: Personalized psychotherapy response
problems.question: Which pretreatment and dynamic features predict treatment benefit causally for a given individual?
problems.justification: Average randomized treatment effects conceal heterogeneous responses.
problems.bottleneck: Confounding of therapy choices and regression to the mean undermine personalization.
problems.direction: Use sequentially randomized trials and prespecified individual treatment rules.
problems.first_test: Show prospective superiority of a personalized allocation policy over standard care.

problems.title: Digital behavioral biomarkers across contexts
problems.question: Can passive behavioral measures track meaningful psychological change without spurious proxies?
problems.justification: Phone and wearable signals are scalable but easily context dependent.
problems.bottleneck: Missingness, socioeconomic confounding and privacy limit validity.
problems.direction: Compare passive markers with repeated validated assessments and cross-device tests.
problems.first_test: Maintain calibration under device switch and changed routine; document consent and privacy.

problems.title: Placebo and context-dependent symptom relief
problems.question: Which learning, expectation and neurobiological mechanisms generate placebo responses in different conditions?
problems.justification: Context can change experienced symptoms and some physiological responses.
problems.bottleneck: Expectancy and natural fluctuations are hard to disentangle.
problems.direction: Factorial designs randomizing information and conditioning with ethical consent.
problems.first_test: Predict placebo response to a novel context from separately measured mechanism variables.

problems.title: Reliable replication across settings
problems.question: Which study features determine whether a reported psychological effect replicates elsewhere?
problems.justification: Large replication projects find heterogeneity in replication outcomes.
problems.bottleneck: Publication selection, analytic flexibility and context sensitivity compound.
problems.direction: Create prospective multi-lab registered replications with variance-component models.
problems.first_test: Predict replication effect distribution before new sites collect data.

problems.title: Measurement invariance of psychological constructs
problems.question: Under what conditions do questionnaires measure the same latent quantity across language, group and time?
problems.justification: Apparent mean differences can result from different item functioning.
problems.bottleneck: Factor models rely on strong assumptions about latent structure and response style.
problems.direction: Fit multigroup item-response models; compare to behavioral anchors and cognitive interviews.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate stable calibrated interpretation on a held-out linguistic group.

problems.title: Causal identification from longitudinal observations
problems.question: Which psychological causal effects can be identified under time-varying confounding and feedback?
problems.justification: Repeated observations alone may not distinguish cause from shared drivers.
problems.bottleneck: Interventions may be endogenous and some confounders unobserved.
problems.direction: Construct explicit causal graphs and sensitivity analyses, followed by ethical randomization.
problems.first_test: Prove identifiability under a stated graph or construct an observationally equivalent counterexample.

problems.title: Robustness to researcher degrees of freedom
problems.question: Which conclusions survive defensible alternative measures, exclusions and statistical models?
problems.justification: Single pipelines can overstate certainty in complex behavioral datasets.
problems.bottleneck: Many valid analyses produce heterogeneous results; selective reporting hides them.
problems.direction: Preregister multiverse analysis and blind key labels until plans are fixed.
problems.first_test: Publish specification-curve distribution and test independent replication predictions.

problems.title: Causal hierarchy of aging mechanisms
problems.question: Which molecular and cellular changes drive functional aging rather than merely track it?
problems.justification: Intervention design requires distinguishing drivers from correlated biomarkers.
problems.bottleneck: Feedback among damage, inflammation and senescence creates reverse causation.
problems.direction: Perform staged perturbations and mediation analysis across genetically heterogeneous models.
problems.first_test: Show a mechanism-specific intervention changes later functional outcomes independent of baseline aging markers.

problems.title: Protective versus harmful senescent cell states
problems.question: Which senescent cells aid repair and which contribute to progressive dysfunction?
problems.justification: Broad senescence removal may also eliminate protective functions.
problems.bottleneck: No universal biomarker separates senescent phenotypes across tissues.
problems.direction: Build spatial single-cell atlases combined with cell-state-selective perturbations.
problems.first_test: Prospectively distinguish repair-promoting from dysfunction-promoting states in a new tissue.

problems.title: Validating biological age as a causal endpoint
problems.question: Do epigenetic and other aging clocks track modifiable biological mechanisms or only correlated exposures?
problems.justification: Intervention trials increasingly rely on surrogate age measures.
problems.bottleneck: Cell mixture changes and differing clock definitions can generate discordant results.
problems.direction: Compare interventions on clocks, functional endpoints and causal mediators.
problems.first_test: Test whether clock change predicts held-out hard functional outcomes independent of chronological age.

problems.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction versus adaptation
problems.question: When are mitochondrial changes causative damage and when are they protective energetic responses?
problems.justification: Mitochondrial physiology affects multiple organs and stress responses.
problems.bottleneck: Biogenesis, reactive oxygen species and quality control vary by tissue and state.
problems.direction: Use tissue-specific perturbations and energetic flux measurement across time.
problems.first_test: Predict when raising respiratory capacity improves versus harms organ resilience.

problems.title: Heterogeneous origins of insulin resistance
problems.question: Which proximal mechanisms explain impaired insulin action in different tissues and individuals?
problems.justification: One clinical phenotype can result from distinct cellular disruptions.
problems.bottleneck: Insulin secretion, hepatic output and peripheral uptake are interdependent.
problems.direction: Compare mechanistic glucose-insulin models with tracer and clamp experiments.
problems.first_test: Recover tissue-specific flux changes under held-out perturbation, not just fasting glucose.

problems.title: Metabolic flexibility under changing demand
problems.question: What controls switching between carbohydrate and lipid oxidation during exercise, fasting and recovery?
problems.justification: Poor adaptability may accompany metabolic disease despite normal resting biomarkers.
problems.bottleneck: Hormone dynamics, substrate availability and mitochondrial flux interact.
problems.direction: Use calorimetry, isotopic tracers and dynamic constrained flux models.
problems.first_test: Forecast substrate-switch time course after a pre-registered meal-exercise perturbation.

problems.title: Neural–hormonal regulation of appetite
problems.question: How do central sensing, gut signals and environmental inputs produce stable or dysregulated energy intake?
problems.justification: Weight regulation reflects multiple compensating behavioral and endocrine loops.
problems.bottleneck: Feedback adapts over time and perceived intake is imprecise.
problems.direction: Combine controlled feeding, repeated hormone profiles and dynamical system identification.
problems.first_test: Predict compensatory hunger and energy expenditure following an intervention.

problems.title: Endocrine responses to chronic stress
problems.question: Why do chronic stress responses diverge among individuals despite similar exposures?
problems.justification: Persistent stress influences immune and metabolic physiology.
problems.bottleneck: Circadian patterns, medications and subjective appraisal confound endocrine trajectories.
problems.direction: Use repeated ambulatory hormone sampling with perturbation-aware state-space models.
problems.first_test: Predict intra-individual phase and amplitude changes under a standardized challenge.

problems.title: Causal neuroimmune signaling paths
problems.question: Which neural-to-immune and immune-to-neural circuits directly control specific inflammatory responses?
problems.justification: Brain and immune systems continuously communicate, but routes are incompletely mapped.
problems.bottleneck: Hormonal and neuronal effects overlap; interventions affect many cell types.
problems.direction: Combine cell-type-specific perturbations and multisite time-resolved signaling.
problems.first_test: Show circuit-specific rescue or loss of a defined immune phenotype.

problems.title: Persistence of maladaptive chronic inflammation
problems.question: What makes low-grade inflammation self-sustaining after initiating triggers are removed?
problems.justification: Persistent inflammation contributes to multiple chronic diseases.
problems.bottleneck: Immune memory, tissue damage and neural inputs form bidirectional loops.
problems.direction: Use causal perturbation of feedback nodes with longitudinal cytokine and cell-state measures.
problems.first_test: Identify a controllable loop whose disruption terminates persistent inflammatory dynamics.

problems.title: Why neuropathic pain becomes persistent
problems.question: Which neuroimmune mechanisms determine transition from transient nociception to chronic neuropathic pain?
problems.justification: Treatments often relieve symptoms incompletely and individual trajectories vary.
problems.bottleneck: Species differences and complex peripheral/central cell interactions.
problems.direction: Combine human longitudinal sensory testing with targeted mechanistic models.
problems.first_test: Predict chronicity from early signals and validate a pathway-specific perturbation.

problems.title: Quantitative autonomic regulation under uncertainty
problems.question: Can coupled sympathetic, parasympathetic and organ responses be predicted during stress and recovery?
problems.justification: Autonomic signaling coordinates rapid multi-organ homeostasis.
problems.bottleneck: Non-invasive observations are partial; baroreflex and respiratory inputs overlap.
problems.direction: Use closed-loop cardiovascular-autonomic system identification with controlled maneuvers.
problems.first_test: Predict unseen orthostatic or respiratory challenge responses with bounded model error.

problems.title: Microvascular autoregulation across organs
problems.question: How do local metabolic, myogenic and neurogenic signals coordinate regional blood flow?
problems.justification: Microcirculatory function is decisive in tissue oxygenation even when systemic measures appear normal.
problems.bottleneck: Resolution limits and intertwined regulatory loops impede causal inference.
problems.direction: Combine organ-specific imaging, oxygen sensing and multiscale perfusion models.
problems.first_test: Predict the spatial redistribution of blood flow after a controlled perfusion change.

problems.title: Mechanistic subtypes of HFpEF
problems.question: Which tissue and cellular mechanisms distinguish clinically meaningful HFpEF subtypes?
problems.justification: Preserved ejection fraction includes heterogeneous structural and metabolic dysfunction.
problems.bottleneck: Comorbid conditions and mixed myocardial cell states prevent a single mechanism.
problems.direction: Integrate cardiac mechanics, proteomics and single-cell profiles into prospective phenotyping.
problems.first_test: Predict differential response to a targeted therapy from subtype assignment.

problems.title: Drivers of pulmonary vascular remodeling
problems.question: Which interacting mechanical, inflammatory and metabolic signals convert adaptation into persistent pulmonary vascular disease?
problems.justification: Vascular remodeling can become self-reinforcing and hard to reverse.
problems.bottleneck: Endothelial signaling and local pressure feedback are difficult to separate.
problems.direction: Combine time-resolved vascular organoids with hemodynamic modeling and perturbations.
problems.first_test: Identify a transition threshold predicting irreversible remodeling in a constrained model.

problems.title: Ventilation–perfusion mismatch adaptation
problems.question: How can individual ventilation and perfusion heterogeneity be inferred and forecast during exertion or lung injury?
problems.justification: Gas exchange efficiency depends on dynamically matched regional air and blood supply.
problems.bottleneck: Regional measurements are sparse and gas exchange has multiple compensating pathways.
problems.direction: Fuse imaging and gas-exchange measurements with mechanistic inverse models.
problems.first_test: Predict changes in oxygenation after posture or exercise challenge under measured uncertainty.

problems.title: Inter-organ circadian synchronization
problems.question: Which signals align peripheral tissue clocks and what causes their age-related desynchronization?
problems.justification: Organ timing coordinates metabolism, immunity and repair.
problems.bottleneck: Behavior, light, feeding and hormones form overlapping synchronizing cues.
problems.direction: Use temporally resolved multi-tissue measurements with selective zeitgeber perturbations.
problems.first_test: Predict phase shifts in a non-target organ after a controlled timing intervention.

problems.title: Gut–brain effects: causation versus correlation
problems.question: Which microbial products causally affect neural and endocrine function in humans?
problems.justification: Observed microbiome–brain associations are not interchangeable with mechanisms.
problems.bottleneck: Diet, medications and immune state confound microbial differences.
problems.direction: Use metabolite-resolved randomized interventions and validated causal mediation.
problems.first_test: Demonstrate an intervention changes a prespecified mechanism and functional endpoint.

problems.title: Sex- and context-dependent physiological response
problems.question: How do hormone state, development and environment change responses to standardized interventions?
problems.justification: Population-average physiological models can miss systematic context effects.
problems.bottleneck: Sampling imbalance and within-person variation prevent robust generalization.
problems.direction: Use repeated-measures factorial designs across defined hormonal contexts.
problems.first_test: Predict interaction effects in a held-out context with uncertainty bounds.

problems.title: Quantifying physiological reserve and resilience
problems.question: Can a state variable quantify an organ's ability to recover from controlled stressors before failure occurs?
problems.justification: Resting biomarkers often overlook reduced functional reserve.
problems.bottleneck: Reserve is latent, multidimensional and highly task dependent.
problems.direction: Construct dynamical recovery metrics and test them with graded standardized perturbations.
problems.first_test: Prospectively rank recovery time and adverse functional outcomes in withheld subjects.

vignettes: Physics: energy control is not gradient control

For a smooth, periodic incompressible unforced flow, the standard Navier–Stokes energy identity is (1/2) d||u||_2^2/dt + nu||grad u||_2^2 = 0. This controls kinetic energy and time-integrated dissipation; it does not automatically control sup-norm vorticity. The vortex-stretching term in three dimensions creates the gap between this estimate and global smoothness. Restricted target: prove a scale-sensitive conditional regularity estimate under an explicit geometric alignment assumption. This is a known starting point, not a solution to P02.

For parallel first-order A→B and A→C with rates k1,k2, measurement of A(t)=A0 exp[-(k1+k2)t] identifies only k1+k2. Adding B(t)=A0 k1/(k1+k2)[1-exp(-(k1+k2)t)] identifies k1 and then k2 under the ideal model. A restricted but rigorous next step for C04 is to derive the Jacobian rank conditions for a multi-intermediate network and design the cheapest measurement breaking each remaining degeneracy.
Genetics: distinguish epistasis from additive effects

With binary perturbations x1,x2, the additive-scale interaction is y11-y10-y01+y00. A nonzero contrast demonstrates statistical interaction on that specified phenotype scale under adequate controls; it does not by itself prove a direct molecular interaction. For G06, estimate higher-order contrasts with hierarchical shrinkage and compare predictions against entirely held-out combinatorial perturbations.

The observational pattern A=Y can arise either when A causes Y or when a hidden U causes both A and Y. These models make identical observational predictions but different do(A) predictions. For PS18, state a causal graph and assumptions, derive identification or construct a counterexample, then design an ethical randomized intervention to distinguish plausible mechanisms.

In a simple effective glucose model dG/dt=u-(k0+kI I)G, keeping I constant identifies only the combination k0+kI I. With two well-measured distinct insulin conditions, kI=(r2-r1)/(I2-I1) and k0=r1-kI I1 under this simplified model. For PH05, extend the analysis to endogenous insulin dynamics and tracer-measured fluxes; do not treat the toy model as a clinical physiological model.
intro: This atlas surveys 100 unresolved, research-relevant questions as of 8 October 2026: 20 each in physics, chemistry, genetics, psychology and physiology, subdivided into 25 areas. “Unsolved” means no complete accepted answer to the stated question; the category includes formal mathematical conjectures, foundational empirical questions and narrower active research challenges. These are not all equally difficult, and many have important partial results.

Each entry includes one or two genuine, directly linked scholarly or authoritative resources describing its scientific context, partial results, gaps or limitations. A review motivates the research question; it does not prove that every variant of a question is unsolved or endorse the proposed experiment. The research directions and first-test criteria are proposed investigative pathways, not claims from the cited authors.

A published model is not a solution merely because it fits a benchmark. A plausible mechanism is not established without appropriate causal tests. A formal proof requires explicit assumptions and independent validation. Computational predictions require out-of-distribution and prospective tests; biomedical and human-subject studies require ethics, data governance and rigorous controls.

The Clay Mathematics Institute noted on 11 September 2026 that the Millennium Prize problem had “apparently been settled” following an announced forced-equation breakdown construction; Clay also noted that evaluation would be deliberately unhurried. This atlas separately lists the still-important unforced global-smoothness question. It does not imply that an independently accepted proof of unforced regularity exists. See R2 and R3.
